Why screen-free play matters

The early years are made for touching, talking and trying. A crayon, a picture and a grown-up nearby are all it takes.

Builds thinking skills

Matching, sorting and counting grow memory, attention and early number sense.

Sparks creativity

Colouring and drawing let children make something that is all their own.

Brings you closer

Every page is made to share: you point, they try, and you cheer together.

Strengthens little hands

Tracing and colouring build the grip and control children need for writing later.

Grows with your child

Three gentle levels. Ages are a guide, not a rule: follow your child’s interest and pace.

Little Explorer

Ages 1–2

Look, point and name. Big friendly pictures and simple choices between two.

Little Learner

Ages 2–3

Match, sort, count to three and spot big and small, with a grown-up close by.

Little Thinker

Ages 3–4

Count to five, finish short patterns, match shadows and put events in order.

Try one of these with me today. No screen needed!

Screen-free activities to try at home

Ten minutes, things you already have, and lots of chatting. Our elephant friend shows the way.

1Ages 1–3

Colour Hunt

Pick a colour. Walk around the room and point to everything that colour. Count them together.

2Ages 2–4

Sock Match

Mix up a few pairs of socks. Find the twins, then talk about which socks are big and which are small.

3Ages 3–4

Shadow Guess

Shine a torch on a toy against the wall. Can your child guess the toy from its shadow?

4Ages 1–4

Draw Your Day

After dinner, each draw one thing you did today. Then tell the story of your pictures together.

For parents

Little swaps for less screen time

1Keep a busy basket of crayons, a book and a puzzle where the tablet usually sits.
2Swap one show a day for one activity page done together.
3Make it a little ritual: the same time and the same cosy spot each day.
4Celebrate every try, not perfect answers. Stop while it is still fun.
